info.title: Penny — Conversational PFM Agent
info.description:
A chat-based spending companion for a US retail bank.

Both agent endpoints stream **newline-delimited JSON**: one complete UI component per line, over HTTP chunked transfer. Read the body line by line and dispatch on each line's `component` key — do not buffer the whole response and parse it once.

Conversation history lives server-side, keyed by session. Echo the `x-session-id` response header on your next request to continue a conversation.

The full component contract, framing rules and client examples are in `docs/API.md`.

get.description: Operational readiness — and the dataset summary the UI chrome displays.

post.description:
Send one customer message and receive a stream of UI components.

Conversation history is **not** part of the request: it is held server-side and keyed by session, so a client cannot replay or rewrite earlier turns. Pass the `x-session-id` header (or `session_id` in the body) returned by a previous call to continue a conversation; omit it to start a new one.

200.description: Newline-delimited JSON over chunked transfer. Each line is one complete UI component identified by its `component` key; read the body line by line and render each line as it arrives. `done` terminates the stream. Consumers must tolerate an unknown `component` value by ignoring or placeholder-rendering it, so a newer server can add components without breaking older clients.

x-session-id.description: Server-side conversation id. Echo it back on the next request to continue the same conversation.

x-request-id.description: Correlation id for this request, also present in server logs.

get.description: The proactive summary Penny offers when a session opens: a real figure from the customer's recent spending plus follow-up intents. Same component stream as `/agent/chat`. A live model call on every request — never cached.
